newsitem.title: JAPAN: COMEX group to meet on Chile warehouses in May.
newsitem.headline: COMEX group to meet on Chile warehouses in May.

text.p: A subcommittee of COMEX's copper advisory committee is scheduled to meet on May 15 to work on delivery rules for the exchange's planned copper warehouses in Chile, said COMEX chairman John Moore.
He also expressed hope that COMEX, a division of the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), would eventually open warehouses in the fast-growing Asian region.

He said the opening of Chilean warehouses would face challenges, such as a one-percent duty on U.S. imports of refined Chilean copper, Chilean value-added tax and ensuring that warehouses meet COMEX standards for security.
He expressed optimism that the one percent duty could be addressed either through Chilean membership in the North American Free Trade Agreement or through legislative means.
"These things are not insurmountable," he said.
He had no target date for opening Chilean warehouses, although he said predictions it would take as long as three years were "outlandish".

He said it was his feeling that, without the one percent import duty, delivery in Chile could initially be made at par with U.S. warehouses. If down the road that presented a problem, it could be fixed at that time, he said.
He added that he was also interested in warehouses in Asia and had recently met with producer and consumer representatives in South Korea.
"My personal goal is to have warehouses in the Pacific rim," he said. "The growth over the next 25 years is going to be astounding in this area of the world."
COMEX's larger rival, the London Metal Exchange, has also expressed interest in opening warehouses in East Asia in addition to its warehouse in Singapore.
Moore was attending a meeting of the International Wrought Copper Council.
